claimed_purpose.text: The bundled using-lwc Skill turns LWC into a proactive memory layer that recalls bounded context and writes back only verified knowledge worth reusing
Turns curated documents into a durable Wiki that compounds instead of being rediscovered from raw chunks on every query

mechanisms.text: Write path: a memory event is a structured capsule with typed semantic fragment kinds (observed, decision, constraint, learned, unresolved, outcome), changes (before/after/reason), evidence references, and inter-event relations. At least one semantic entry is required.

Portable memory archives let agents package and merge a wiki between stores; imports stage a resumable merge; whole-store overwrite requires separate human confirmation; existing memory is never replaced implicitly

Search is lexical and deterministic (no vector database); supports explicit auditable document weights and query-specific feedback fingerprints for reranking; neither mechanism can surface unrelated content
Conflict/supersession: corrections invalidate related conclusions transitively including answers depending on a changed question; unrelated conclusions remain fresh; cyclic references are rejected
Agents are instructed to read a designated memory file at the start of substantive work; this file holds a concise project map, documentation map, wiki entry points, and maintenance triggers.
Retrieval ranking is adjusted by two persisted tables: retrieval_weights (manual per-document boosts) and retrieval_feedback (per-query-fingerprint signals), both with provenance tracking.
Two scopes isolating knowledge: project (nearest project Wiki) and global (reusable across projects); writes always target one explicit store, no implicit cross-project citations or links
Retrieve policy: agents search the LWC Wiki with a scoped search command, then open only relevant pages and current source/code evidence — adaptive retrieval rather than always-load.
Retrieve path: full-text search via FTS5 with BM25 ranking (weights: event_type 2.0, context 4.0, content 1.0); filtered by max_age_days window with protected-event override.
The companion Skill (using-lwc) implements a proactive memory layer: recalls bounded context, keeps project and global knowledge separate, writes back only verified knowledge
Plan and Todo isolate lifecycle context by Agent session and, where supported, by subagent; each Agent sees only explicitly tracked work for its opaque context
Durable Discussion records preserve visible clarification Q/A in SQLite with granular corrections and evidence-linked summaries (new in 0.18.0)
Search is lexical (FTS5 contentless table), not semantic/vector; an empty result does not prove knowledge is absent.
SQLite is the canonical store; Markdown, full-text indexes, and optional graph stores are rebuildable projections
Forget / archive policy: agents must archive before permanently deleting brain knowledge.
Guarded deletion: sources with citations and pages with inbound links are refused removal
Secrets must never be written to the memory store.

ledger.claim: LWC stores persistent knowledge in SQLite as the canonical store; Markdown, full-text indexes, and optional graph stores are rebuildable projections, not canonical
ledger.quote: SQLite is canonical. Markdown, full-text indexes, and optional graph stores are rebuildable projections. Agents update knowledge through the CLI; successful operations return structured JSON that can be audited and resumed.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Temporal memory is a curated event log (normalized, not raw transcripts), separate from the Wiki which holds current stable knowledge — two distinct persistence layers
ledger.quote: Events are normalized rather than stored as raw chat transcripts, and similar events are never silently merged.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget/delete is guarded: pages with inbound links and sources with citations are refused for deletion; no silent removal
ledger.quote: Use source remove <id> and page remove <id> for guarded deletion: sources with citations and pages with inbound links are refused.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Conflict resolution fails closed: same-entity revision conflicts in changesets do not overwrite either side and there is no automatic merge
ledger.quote: a same-entity revision conflict fails without overwriting either side... There is no force or automatic merge.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Knowledge isolation is per-scope (project vs global); writes always target one explicit store; no implicit cross-project citations or links
ledger.quote: Writes always target one explicit store. LWC never creates implicit cross-project citations or links.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval is page-first (maintained Wiki answers) before raw source evidence; agents expand to source only when a claim needs verification
ledger.quote: Search is page-first and source-grounded. Agents retrieve maintained answers first, then open exact source evidence when a claim needs verification.
ledger.locator: README.md § Quick Start § 4. Query the accumulated Wiki
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Scaffold: the using-lwc Skill provides instructions that tell the Agent how to use the memory system — when to recall, how to write back only verified knowledge, how to keep scopes separate
ledger.quote: The bundled using-lwc Skill turns LWC into a proactive memory layer. It recalls bounded context, keeps project and global knowledge separate, integrates sources, preserves citations, and writes back only verified knowledge worth reusing.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: LongMemEval-S retrieval baseline (v0.18.5, 500 questions, lexical retrieval only, no model-led curation or weight tuning): Recall@5 95.11%, Recall@10 97.66%, MRR 0.8837
ledger.quote: This is an untuned retrieval baseline, not a ceiling on LWC's effectiveness over continued use... Recall@5 | 95.11% (447/470) ... MRR | 0.883668
ledger.locator: README.md § Benchmark Suite § LongMemEval-S retrieval results (v0.18.5)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Multi-machine sync reconciles project or global memory over SSH; merge preserves unique objects from both sides; conflicts returned as bounded packets for explicit resolution; sessions are durable and resumable
ledger.quote: Sync reconciles project memory, global memory, or both over SSH while keeping semantic Wiki state separate from Git publication. Merge preserves unique objects from both sides; conflicts are returned as bounded packets for explicit resolution. Sessions are durable and resumable.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Plan and Todo isolation is per Agent session (and per subagent where the host exposes it); each Agent sees only explicitly tracked work for its opaque context
ledger.quote: Bounded lifecycle context isolates Plan and Todo progress by Agent session and, where the host exposes it, by subagent. Each Agent sees only explicitly tracked work for its opaque context.
ledger.locator: README.md § Durable Todo and current Plan
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: LWC exposes memory retrieval and discussion persistence over MCP; the server itself is read-only for Wiki memory and CodeGraph, with writes confined to the discussion_apply action in project SQLite
ledger.quote: "annotations": {"readOnlyHint": true, "destructiveHint": false, "idempotentHint": true, "openWorldHint": false}
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory retrieve is adaptive by scope (project vs global) and mode (memory/code/all), not always-retrieve; absent a store the response degrades to state:unavailable rather than failing
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Discussion persistence uses project SQLite with CAS and stable IDs; the 'current' and 'history' actions support recovering state after context compaction
ledger.quote: Recover current bound discussion after compaction.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The store path for project memory is .lwc/wiki.db under the project directory
ledger.quote: let store = crate::scope::StorePath::new(Scope::Project, project.join(".lwc/wiki.db"));

ledger.claim: MCP server identifies itself as 'lwc' with version from CARGO_PKG_VERSION
ledger.quote: "serverInfo": {"name": "lwc", "version": env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")}
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Sources (raw documents) and pages (curated wiki entries) are stored in separate SQLite tables, representing a two-tier architecture: a raw log layer and a curated memory layer
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Deletion from the store is hard deletion: rows are removed from sources/pages, FTS index, retrieval_weights, retrieval_feedback, and search_spans are deactivated — there is no soft-delete or hide-at-retrieve path visible in this file
ledger.quote: deactivate_search_spans(&tx, "source", &id.to_string())?;
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval ranking is influenced by persisted retrieval_weights and retrieval_feedback, meaning past retrieval events can affect future ranking
ledger.quote: apply_retrieval_state(&self.conn, &tokens, &mut results)?;
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: All mutations are appended to an operations log (record_operation), providing an audit trail separate from the entity tables
ledger.quote: record_operation(&tx, "page_put", &input.slug, &json!({ "created": !existed }))?;
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: The store carries a 'scope' field on every response, indicating that isolation boundaries exist at the store level; the isolation mechanism (per-user, per-agent, per-character) is not described in this file
ledger.quote: scope: self.scope.clone(),
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Graph relations are written with typed edges, provenance, confidence, and source citations, and trigger async graph projection work after each write.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Graph relations can be retracted (deleted) from the store with a recorded reason, and also trigger a graph projection update.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval weights persist per (target, provenance) and are upserted, allowing existing weights to be overwritten rather than duplicated.
ledger.quote:
ON CONFLICT(target_type, target_identifier, provenance)
                 DO UPDATE SET weight = excluded.weight,
                               reason = excluded.reason,
                               updated_at = excluded.updated_at
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval feedback (relevant/irrelevant signal) is stored per query fingerprint and target, upserted per provenance, influencing ranking for matching queries.
ledger.quote:
ON CONFLICT(query_fingerprint, target_type, target_identifier, provenance)
                 DO UPDATE SET signal = excluded.signal,
                               reason = excluded.reason,
                               updated_at = excluded.updated_at
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Graph re-ranking is applied at retrieval time using stored graph structure (links, shared sources, neighbors); it does not require a separate retrieval call — it modifies ranks on already-retrieved results.
ledger.quote:
explanation.signals.graph_match = explanation
                .graph_seeds
                .iter()
                .map(|seed| seed.contribution)
                .fold(0.0, f64::max)
                .clamp(0.0, 1.0);
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: All store mutations are accompanied by operation log records in the same transaction, creating a durable audit log alongside curated memory state.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Store isolation is per scope and database path; all graph, retrieval, and ingest operations are namespaced by these two identifiers.
ledger.quote:
scope: self.scope.clone(),
            database: self.database_string(),
ledger.locator: impl Store / retrieval_weight_set (and all other mutation responses)
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Semantic relations (SUPPORTS, CONTRADICTS, REFINES, SUPERSEDES, CAUSES, DEPENDS_ON) are written to a persistent SQLite store with upsert conflict resolution, updating confidence, provenance, reason, and source links on re-assertion.
ledger.quote:
INSERT INTO semantic_relations(
                id, relation_type, from_identifier, to_identifier,
                confidence, provenance, reason, source_ids_json, created_at, updated_at
             ) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3, ?4, ?5, ?6, ?7, ?8, {TIMESTAMP_SQL}, {TIMESTAMP_SQL})
             ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
                confidence = excluded.confidence,
                provenance = excluded.provenance,
                reason = excluded.reason,
                source_ids_json = excluded.source_ids_json,
                updated_at = excluded.updated_at
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget/retract is a hard DELETE from semantic_relations, not a soft hide; the operation is logged with a reason via record_operation.
ledger.quote: tx.execute("DELETE FROM semantic_relations WHERE id = ?1", [&id])?
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Spans become stale (and are refused at retrieval) when a document's content fingerprint changes or the active flag is unset, preventing retrieval of outdated memory anchors.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval ranking is adjusted at query time by two persistent stores: per-document manual weights and per-(query-fingerprint, document) feedback signals, both with user-provided provenance taking priority.
ledger.quote:
let weights = load_effective_weights(conn)?;
    let feedback = load_effective_feedback(conn, &query_fingerprint(query_tokens))?;
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Query fingerprinting is SHA-256 over the ordered, separator-delimited token list, making feedback keyed to the specific token set rather than raw query string.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Memory is stored as curated events with typed semantic fragments, not a raw message log.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Write idempotency is enforced via SHA-256 fingerprint keyed on request_id; conflicting re-use of the same request_id with different content is rejected.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Retrieval uses FTS5 BM25 ranking adjusted by user feedback score; events older than max_age_days are excluded unless protected.
ledger.quote:
bm25(memory_fts, 0.0, 2.0, 4.0, 1.0) AS lexical_rank
                 FROM memory_fts
                 JOIN memory_events e ON e.id = memory_fts.event_id
                 WHERE memory_fts MATCH ?1
                   AND (
                       JULIANDAY(e.occurred_at) >= JULIANDAY('now', '-' || ?2 || ' days')
                       OR {MEMORY_EVENT_PROTECTED_SQL}
                   )
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget by age: events older than max_age_days are hard-deleted unless pinned, unresolved, or in an unresolved contradiction.
ledger.quote:
WHERE JULIANDAY(e.occurred_at) < JULIANDAY('now', '-' || ?1 || ' days')
           AND NOT ({MEMORY_EVENT_PROTECTED_SQL})
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget by capacity: oldest unprotected events are hard-deleted until logical_bytes ≤ max_bytes.
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Hints are emitted post-write for relation-review, cluster density, aged-unresolved items, and storage pressure, with a 7-day cooldown per candidate key.
ledger.quote: STRFTIME('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now', '+7 days')
ledger.label: measured

ledger.claim: Forget path: ordinary expired events are deleted by retention policy enforcement on each `remember` call and by `memory maintain`; protected events (pinned, unresolved, open contradicts) are never deleted and will cause recording to fail if capacity is exceeded.
ledger.quote: Ordinary expired history is deleted. Events with pinned=true , an unresolved fragment, or an explicit contradicts relation not closed by resolves are protected. If protected history leaves insufficient capacity, recording fails rather than deleting it.
